subject: EXTERNAL: Bridgenet demo — chunked JSON boundary drain + proxy handoff causing pauses
messages:
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@bridgenet.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lyle <tom.lyle@bridgenet.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Live API intermittency during demo — urgent

Marcus —

We just ran a customer-facing demo (region: us-east-1) and saw repeated pauses in the live response stream. The UI shows a freeze for ~6–12s, then a burst of tokens catches up. On a couple of runs the client saw a 504 and reconnected, causing duplicated completions. This is blocking our procurement sign-off today.

Attached are server logs from the demo and the client-side request IDs. Key observations from our side:
- Pauses always start after ~1.6k tokens on longer prompts.
- Reconnects lead to partial JSON objects (truncated chunk boundaries) which our renderer treats as a hard failure.
- There are a few 502/504 traces in front of your endpoint in our edge logs.

Can you please triage immediately — we have an executive call at 18:00 PT and need a mitigation plan.

Attached: bridgenet_demo_logs_20280515.txt (small excerpt + request ids)

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Gupta
Senior Product Manager, BridgeNet
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@bridgenet.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Live API intermittency during demo — urgent

Aisha — thanks for the fast report and the logs. I'm pulling in infra and support.

Quick asks so we can triage before the exec call:
- Can you paste one full request-id (x-request-id) from the run that shows the 6–12s pause?
- Which client SDK and connection mode (chunked transfer / websocket) was used for the demo?
- If you can, share the exact edge load-balancer (vendor/version) and any proxy timeout/keepalive settings you have.

Initial plan: Karthik will look at the token-level traces and server-side flush behaviour; Sean will check our ingress for proxy handoffs and any 502/504 anomalies. I'll schedule a short war-room and loop in Vivek if this looks like it needs exec attention.

I'll propose a 30-minute troubleshooting window at 10:30 PT — is that viable for you?

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupten@bridgenet.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Live API intermittency during demo — urgent

Marcus / Sean — quick triage notes (token-level traces attached):

What I've observed from request ids Marcus pulled from Aisha's logs:
- Server-side logs show continuous generation but our response flushes are being coalesced by an upstream proxy around the ~1.5–1.8k token point. That aligns with the client seeing a long pause followed by a catch-up.
- There are intermittent 502 responses from a layer that appears to be doing proxy handoffs (likely customer's ELB -> CDN -> edge). When a handoff occurs mid-stream, the connection is torn and the client reconnects, sometimes receiving partially-complete chunked frames.
- Chunk boundary misalignment is visible (partial JSON object per chunk) which explains the renderer failure.

Immediate mitigations to propose to customer (low risk / short lead):
1) Reduce server-side chunk coalescing frequency (flush smaller chunks more often) so upstream proxies see steady traffic and are less likely to consider the connection idle.
2) Recommend customer's proxy/ELB set keepalive and idle timeouts higher than our longest expected burst (we should provide specific numbers).
3) As a short-term workaround, enable client-side tolerant parsing to merge truncated chunks until the stream completes.

I prepared a tiny patch that forces more frequent flushes on the currently-serving runtime path (non-invasive, toggled by header). Patch: proxy_keepalive_tweak.patch

I'll attach token traces and a snippet that shows the 502 handoff timestamps. If customer confirms their edge config we can recommend exact timeout values.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupten@bridgenet.com>, Tom Lyle <tom.lyle@bridgenet.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T10:28:00Z
Subject: EXTERNAL: Escalation: BridgeNet demo interruptions — exec sync

Team — flagging this for exec visibility. BridgeNet is in procurement for a dedicated commitment and this behavior during a live demo is P0 for them.

Summary of current status:
- Customer saw repeated ~6–12s pauses in live response stream; reconnects sometimes produced partial JSON chunks and 504s.
- Karthik's analysis points to upstream proxy handoff/keepalive mismatch combined with our chunk coalescing behaviour. Karthik has a patch that forces more frequent flushes and can be toggled via a header for BridgeNet only.
- Immediate ask: can we ship the toggle to BridgeNet (non-breaking) and provide recommended keepalive/timeout values for their edge?

Aisha — we can flip the header on for your account for immediate mitigation; we will also request your edge config (ELB/CDN/NGINX) so we can provide specific values.

Vivek — want to keep you aware in case the customer requests an exec-level SLA concession. Sean, please prepare the ingress/edge 502/504 timeline for the war-room.

Marcus
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@bridgenet.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lyle <tom.lyle@bridgenet.com>, Support <support@bridgenet.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T14:48:00Z
Subject: Re: EXTERNAL: Escalation: BridgeNet demo interruptions — exec sync

Marcus / team — thanks for the quick loop. We deployed the header toggle on a staging call and the stream now flows with sub-second pauses instead of multi-second stalls. That looks promising.

We still want an exec sync to confirm root cause and next steps for production. Procurement has put the purchase on hold until we get an unequivocal remediation plan. Can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow at 11:00 PT? Also, we'll share our ELB config and traces (drive link above).

Appreciate the fast support — please keep me posted if any temporary SLA credits or escalation notes are needed for procurement.

— Aisha
